label: the filter is never reset
why: EQUIVALENT ONLY BECAUSE `GenericIIR`'s OWN CONSTRUCTOR ALREADY RESETS. `src/dsp/FloatIIR.cpp`'s GenericIIR(...) ends with `reset();`, so by the time this line runs every field that reset writes already holds the value it would write: both history buffers are zero and both positions are at their start. Calling it a second time is idempotent, so removing the call leaves the filter in a state no comparison can distinguish. THE OBJECT'S CALL IS REAL AND IS REPRODUCED -- `call _ZN10GenericIIRIfdE5resetEv` at 0x1073d, with its own R_386_PC32 -- and what is untestable is only whether removing it changes anything here. Registered rather than deleted because the equivalence is CONDITIONAL: let GenericIIR's constructor stop resetting, or give reset() a field it does not idempotently rewrite, and this becomes a real defect that will then be CAUGHT and reported MIScounted -- which is the notification this entry exists to produce.
